subject: Biology
central_question: How are microbes used in food, industry, waste treatment, energy production, biological control and soil fertility to improve human welfare?
in_scope_units: Diversity and ubiquity of microbes and growth of microbial colonies.
Microbes in household foods and fermented products.
Industrial production of beverages, antibiotics, organic acids, enzymes and bioactive molecules.
Primary and secondary sewage treatment, BOD, activated sludge and anaerobic digestion.
Methanogens, biogas and the structure and use of biogas plants.
Biological control of pests and plant diseases using predators, bacteria, fungi and viruses.
Biofertilisers based on nitrogen-fixing bacteria, mycorrhizae and cyanobacteria.
banned_topics: Detailed pathogenesis and immunity from Human Health and Disease.
Detailed recombinant DNA cloning methods and transgenic crop construction.
Industrial chemical engineering specifications beyond the fermentor and treatment descriptions in the chapter.

known_pitfalls.correction: Many microbes are useful in food production, industry, sewage treatment, biogas, biocontrol and biofertilisation.

known_pitfalls.claim: Primary sewage treatment is a microbial process.
known_pitfalls.correction: Primary treatment is mainly physical filtration and sedimentation; secondary treatment is the main biological stage.

known_pitfalls.claim: A high BOD indicates clean water.
known_pitfalls.correction: Higher BOD means more oxygen would be consumed by microbes and therefore indicates greater organic pollution.

known_pitfalls.claim: Bt kills every organism in the field.
known_pitfalls.correction: Bacillus thuringiensis is used against particular insect larvae and can leave many non-target organisms unharmed.

known_pitfalls.claim: Biofertilisers directly supply synthetic fertiliser salts.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are living organisms that enrich soil nutrient quality through processes such as nitrogen fixation or improved phosphorus uptake.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Exercises 2-4 on gases, LAB and fermented foods.
Use NCERT Exercises 5-6 and 12 on antibiotics and industrial bioactive products.
Use NCERT Exercises 7-8 and the BOD data in Exercise 11 for sewage treatment.
Use NCERT Exercise 9 for methanogens and biogas.
Finish with NCERT Exercises 10 and 15 for biocontrol and biofertilisers.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 1 to 15 and cover household products, industrial products, sewage, BOD, biogas, biocontrol and biofertilisers.
